discovery: Realization of strongly interacting Fermi gases and the BEC-BCS crossover to fermionic superfluidity

nominees.name: Rudolf Grimm
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Christophe Salomon
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire Kastler Brossel, ENS-PSL, CNRS, Paris, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / ultracold quantum gases
motivation: Using Feshbach resonances in ultracold lithium-6, the nominees turned a dilute Fermi gas into a fully tunable model of strongly interacting quantum matter. Thomas observed the first strongly interacting, hydrodynamically expanding Fermi gas (2002). Grimm's group created a Bose-Einstein condensate of molecules (2003), then mapped the crossover to BCS-type pairing via collective modes and a direct measurement of the pairing gap (2004). Salomon's group produced molecular condensates and precision measurements of the universal unitary-gas equation of state. Together these experiments established the BEC-BCS crossover, connecting molecular condensation and Cooper pairing in a single, controllable system, with universal behaviour shared by neutron-star matter and the quark-gluon plasma. The work founded a field: precision tests of many-body theory, near-perfect fluidity, and today's single-atom-resolved studies of pairing and emergence.
